name: Blending Flower Water
description: Blending flower water prepares an optimal nutrient and hydrating solution that keeps cut flowers fresh and prevents bacterial blockages or salt scorch. The process requires mixing flower food powder at exactly 10 g/L (such as 8 g in 800 ml water) using warm water heated to 41 °C.

learned_parameters.label: Water Volume
learned_parameters.rationale: Setting water volume to 800 ml paired with 8 g of powder achieved a 100 sub-score for concentration and an overall score of 100.0 (attempts #5 and #10). Reducing volume to 500 ml with 8 g caused over-concentration (sub-score 6, attempt #6, overall 43.4), whereas increasing volume to 1050 ml caused under-concentration (sub-score 64, attempt #8, overall 78.1). Measured: Total score by value: 500 ml -> 43.4, 800 ml -> 8.1, 800 ml -> 40.0, 800 ml -> 40.7, 800 ml -> 41.5, 800 ml -> 48.1, 800 ml -> 100.0, 1050 ml -> 78.1.

learned_parameters.label: Flower Food Powder
learned_parameters.rationale: 8 g of flower food powder dissolved in 800 ml water creates a concentration of 10 g/L, scoring a perfect 100 for preservative concentration and 100.0 overall (attempts #5 and #10). Lower doses (2 g scored 1 in attempt #9; 4 g scored 14 in attempts #1–#3) led to starvation and bacterial growth, while higher doses (12 g scored 14 in attempt #4; 16 g scored 0 in attempt #7) caused chemical burn, confirming Floralife Research dosing guidelines. Measured: Total score by value: 2 g -> 40.7, 4 g -> 8.1, 4 g -> 41.5, 4 g -> 48.1, 8 g -> 43.4, 8 g -> 78.1, 8 g -> 100.0, 12 g -> 48.1, 16 g -> 40.0.

learned_parameters.label: Water Temperature
learned_parameters.rationale: Water at 41 °C produced a perfect sub-score of 100 across attempts #3, #4, #5, #7, #8, #9, and #10, reaching an overall score of 100.0 in attempts #5 and #10. Colder water at 16 °C scored 0 (attempt #1, overall 8.1), and warm water at 35 °C scored 84 (attempt #2, overall 41.5). According to UMass Amherst Extension, warm water around 40–43 °C has lower viscosity and fewer trapped gas bubbles, facilitating rapid stem uptake. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 41 °C. Tried 16 °C (sub-score 0) to 41 °C (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 35 °C and 41 °C.

control_effects.effect: Determines the dilution of the flower food powder. With 8 g of powder, 500 ml made the solution hypertonic (attempt #6: concentration sub-score 6, score 43.4), 1050 ml diluted it too much (attempt #8: concentration sub-score 64, score 78.1), and 800 ml hit the exact target ratio (attempt #5: concentration sub-score 100, score 100.0). Measured: Total score by value: 500 ml -> 43.4, 800 ml -> 8.1, 800 ml -> 40.0, 800 ml -> 40.7, 800 ml -> 41.5, 800 ml -> 48.1, 800 ml -> 100.0, 1050 ml -> 78.1.

Directly adjusts preservative and carbohydrate concentration when combined with water volume. At 800 ml water, 2 g scored 1 (attempt #9, score 40.7), 4 g scored 14 (attempt #3, score 48.1), 8 g scored 100 (attempt #5, score 100.0), 12 g scored 14 (attempt #4, score 48.1), and 16 g scored 0 (attempt #7, score 40.0). Measured: Total score by value: 2 g -> 40.7, 4 g -> 8.1, 4 g -> 41.5, 4 g -> 48.1, 8 g -> 43.4, 8 g -> 78.1, 8 g -> 100.0, 12 g -> 48.1, 16 g -> 40.0.

Controls the Water Temperature sub-score and stem rehydration speed. Increasing temperature from 16 °C (attempt #1: sub-score 0, score 8.1) to 35 °C (attempt #2: sub-score 84, score 41.5) and 41 °C (attempt #3: sub-score 100, score 48.1) eliminated cold water embolisms. Measured: Best sub-score 100/100 at 41 °C. Tried 16 °C (sub-score 0) to 41 °C (sub-score 100). Sub-score stayed at or above 80 between 35 °C and 41 °C.
4 g / 800 ml resulted in 14/100, feedback confirmed it is too dilute. Measured: Relation 'Preservative Concentration' depends on several controls together; best sub-score 100/100.

steps: Measure 800 ml of clean water into the vase or mixing container.
Heat or adjust the water temperature to exactly 41 °C.
Weigh out 8 g of flower food powder.
Add the 8 g of powder into the 800 ml of warm water and stir until fully dissolved to achieve the target 10 g/L preservative concentration.
caveats: Preservative concentration depends on the ratio of water volume to food powder, not on powder amount alone.
Water colder than 35 °C inhibits rehydration and risks vascular embolisms in stem vessels.
Over-concentrating flower food draws water backward out of stems via osmotic pressure, scorching petal margins.
Under-dosing flower food starves blooms of carbohydrates and allows bacterial proliferation.
'Preservative Concentration' depends on several controls together, not one alone.

problems.problem: The nutrient solution is too dilute; bacteria thrive while the opening blossoms starve of carbohydrates.
problems.fix: Increase flower food powder to match the 10 g/L ratio (e.g., increase powder to 8 g for 800 ml of water, or reduce excess water volume).

problems.problem: The water is too cold; viscous water and trapped air embolisms delay stem rehydration.
problems.fix: Raise the water temperature to 41 °C before mixing and placing stems.
